description.summary: HDR and adaptive sync capability for wlr-output-management heads

protocol.description:
An extension of wlr-output-management-unstable-v1 for what that protocol cannot say: whether a head can be driven in HDR, whether it is, the luminance SDR content is shown at while it is, and whether the head can do adaptive sync at all (wlr-output-management reports only whether it is on).
Every object here hangs off a wlr-output-management object. A head extension describes a zwlr_output_head_v1, and a configuration head extension adds requests to a zwlr_output_configuration_head_v1, which are applied atomically with the rest of that configuration when it is applied.
wlr-output-management re-creates its heads whenever anything about the outputs changes, so a head extension describes one snapshot of one head. A client wanting current values asks for a new extension for each head of each new snapshot.
This is a wlRIX-specific protocol, not a standard.

interface.name: wlrix_output_color_manager_v1
interface.description: A global. Binding it alone does nothing; extensions are created for individual heads.

request.name: get_head

description.summary: describe a head's HDR and adaptive sync capability

request.description:
Create an extension for a head. The compositor sends every event of the new object immediately, closed by done.
Asking twice for the same head is allowed, and gives two independent objects. Asking for a head that has since been finished gives an object that reports nothing supported.

request.name: get_configuration_head

description.summary: extend a head in a pending configuration

request.description: Create an extension for a head the client has enabled in a pending configuration, to stage HDR changes that are applied along with it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects already created from it remain valid.

interface.name: wlrix_output_color_head_v1

description.summary: one head's HDR and adaptive sync state

interface.description: Describes the head it was created for, as it was when created. Every event is sent once, then done.

event.name: hdr_supported
event.description: 1 when both the connector and the panel can be driven in HDR (PQ / BT.2020), 0 otherwise. A head that cannot do HDR refuses a configuration enabling it.

event.name: hdr
event.description: 1 when the head is being driven in HDR now, 0 when it is in SDR.

event.name: sdr_white_level
event.description: The luminance, in cd/m², that SDR white is shown at while the head is in HDR. Reported whether or not HDR is on, since it is what the head will use when it is turned on.

event.name: luminance
event.description: What the panel says it can show, from its EDID. Only sent for a head that supports HDR. min is in units of 0.0001 cd/m², so an OLED black is representable; max is in cd/m².

event.name: adaptive_sync_supported
event.description: 1 when the head can do adaptive sync (variable refresh rate), 0 otherwise. A head that cannot refuses a configuration enabling it.

event.name: done
event.description: Sent after the other events. Nothing follows it.

interface.name: wlrix_output_color_configuration_head_v1

description.summary: HDR changes staged in a configuration

interface.description: Requests made here are staged in the configuration the head belongs to, and applied, or refused, atomically with it. Anything not requested is left as it is.

entry.name: invalid_sdr_white_level
entry.summary: the SDR white level is outside the accepted range

request.name: set_hdr
request.description: 1 to drive the head in HDR, 0 for SDR. Enabling HDR on a head that does not support it makes the configuration fail.

request.name: set_sdr_white_level

description.summary: set the reference white for SDR content

request.description: In cd/m², from 80 to 500 inclusive. A value outside that range is a protocol error.
